name: SquareLaw.sum_eq_nextDatum
summary: Apply the partner identity of the square law to the block partners of the point function at (x; 0) (`partner_block`), and use the GL-equivariance of L and L′ to move the blocks to the standard ones.

steps.claim: Substitute y ↦ −y and write the left side as an average over the n × b matrices (a constant expectation).
steps.lean: rw [← neg_bijective.sum_comp, ← Fintype.expect_const (ι := Matrix n b R) (_ * _), expect]

steps.claim: Split the sums over block matrices (`sum_eq_sum_fromRows`) and distribute.
Compare term by term, for each s (an n × b matrix) and x.
The partner identity (3) of h for the block partners of the point function at w (`partner_block`) (t), and the equivariances of L (l) and L′ (r) rewritten through the reindexing by σ.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨t, l, r⟩ := h.partners _ _ (partner_block σ χ (Pi.single w 1)),
    (submatrix_mul_equiv _ (w.fromCols 1) id (.refl _) σ.symm ▸ h.left_mul · _),
    ((fromRows 1 (-w)).submatrix_mul_equiv _ σ.symm (.refl _) id ▸ h.right_mul · _)

steps.claim: Rewrite the sums over matrices and over invertible matrices (each invertible square matrix weighted by χ⁻¹(det)), using the block decompositions.
steps.lean:
simp_all [reindex_equiv (Matrix.reindex σ (.refl _)),
    sum_eq_sum_fromRows (N := a), ↓reindex_equiv (Matrix.reindex (.refl _) σ),
    ← fun m [Fintype m] (f : Matrix m m R → ℂ) ↦ sum_of_injective _ Units.val_injective _ (fun u ↦
    (χ u.det)⁻¹ * f u) (by simp [mt ·.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det.2 ·]) (by tauto), ← mul_sum, -mul_ite]

steps.claim: Evaluate L at the block matrix (1 s; 0 1) and L′ at 1 by the equivariances l and r; the remaining matrix identities hold by unfolding swapFirstTwo.
steps.lean:
erw [congr(L $(?_)).trans (l (.mk'' (fromBlocks 1 s 0 1) _)), congr(L' $(?_)).trans (r 1)] <;>
    simp_all [← ext_iff, w, σ, swapFirstTwo]; grind
